items.title: Presentations
Delegations
Jen Hutton, CEO, Women's Crisis Services of Waterloo Region
notes:
Jen Hutton, CEO, Women's Crisis Services of Waterloo Region introduced herself and the delegates listed under items 6.2-6.4., Amy Hachborn, Waterloo Regional Police Services, Christine Taylor, Sexual/Assault Domestic Violence Treatment Centre, and Lisa Akey, Camino Wellbeing + Mental Health. They expressed support for declaring intimate partner violence (IPV) as an epidemic, a copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

The group presented on the Family Violence Project Waterloo Region's various initiatives and partnerships. They highlighted the inquest of the deaths of Carol Culleton, Anastasia Kuzyk and Nathalie Warnerdam as well as Waterloo Regional Police Service statistics on IPV. They also highlighted the impact of the Women's Crisis Services of Waterloo Region, which includes providing shelter to 4,875 clients, both women and children. They noted that the Camino Wellbeing and Mental Health organization has supported more than 1,800 affected by IPV per year and that the Sexual Assault/Domestic Violence Treatment Centre assisted 140 IPV survivors access counselling.

The group provided various reasons to declare IPV an epidemic, such that the declaration would demonstrate Council support for the victims of IPV and their families.

In response to the Committee, J. Hutton confirmed the significant impact on minimizing IPV through prevention outreach, specifically when working youth. She noted that funding is primarily sourced through donations. J. Hutton further noted that the helplines provided in the attachment under 6.1 are applicable for all local municipalities and not just the cities that are listed.

In response to the Committee, Connie Macdonald, Chief Communications & Strategy Officer agreed that IPV should be added as a priority to the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan and she confirmed that the current plan is to discuss it at the next steering committee later this year.

notes: Sarah Shafiq, Director of Advocacy, Research & Outreach, Coalition of Muslim Women of KW, expressed support for the proposed motion under item 8.1.4 CAO-EDI-23-003, Amendment to Code of Use By-Law (13-050) to Prohibit Harassing/Discriminatory Behaviour on Regional Premises. She also expressed appreciation for the collaboration with Regional Staff and various organizations to ensure the proper treatment of marginalized community members across the Region. She noted that the proposed amendment would align with both the Ontario Human Rights Code and with many other municipalities in the province. She further noted that the harassment and discriminatory behaviour experienced by equity seeking groups is not being addressed by the Criminal Code, therefore, the proposed amendment would aid in the safety and well-being of these individuals.

items.title: Maedith Radlein, Kitchener
notes: Maedith Radlein provided a delegation in support of 8.1.4 CAO-EDI-23-003, Amendment to Code of Use By-Law (13-050) to Prohibit Harassing/Discriminatory Behaviour on Regional Premises. She expressed that she is fearful of the hate she feels in the community and that elected officials must establish policies or by-laws to protect against this hate. CSD-HOU-23-026, Incentives for Affordable Housing: Report on the Work of the Intra-municipal Working Group
notes:
P. Sweeney introduced Jeffery Schumacher, Manager, Affordable Housing Development, a copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. J. Schumacher highlighted the Intra-municipal Affordable Housing Incentives Working Group initiatives, which include environmental scan, online surveys and parking study and parking cost case studies. He also highlighted the survey results that identified several factors related to affordable housing, such as CMHC funding programs. He further highlighted that the next steps for Staff which includes communicating the incentive survey results, parking report, and park case studies with area municipalities. 

In response to the Committee, J. Schumacher explained that a timeline has not been established as some initiatives are not within the scope of the Region. P. Sweeney elaborated by adding that the report identifies tools and resources that can be implemented to establish these initiatives with our Municipal partners. 

Responding to the Committee, J. Schumacher confirmed that Regional Staff have been collaborating with Township Staff to improve affordable housing options in the Townships which include providing support to Township Staff when submitting CMHC applications. He further confirmed that area municipalities were involved in development of the surveys and analysis to ensure that it is beneficial for the area municipalities. 

The Committee expressed concern related consistency across the Region by ensuring that transit, parking and accessibility are considerations for developments projects. The Committee further expressed concern with the parking study as larger families may require larger vehicles and driveways to accommodate their needs.

In response to the Committee, Ryan Pettipiere, Director, Housing Services, elaborated that the identified initiatives would need to be applied on a project specific basis and that Townships may be utilizing some of the incentives at the area municipal level, however, Regional Staff support may help to enhance these initiatives.

Received for information.

items.title: CSD-HOU-23-024, The Plan to End Chronic Homelessness Key Findings
notes:
Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Housing Services, introduced Peter Phillips, Supervisor, Quality Assurance & Integration, Ben Balfour, Overlap Associates, Aleksandra Petrovic, Social Development Centre Waterloo Region, and Fran Truong, Community Services Housing Representative, that provided an update on the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, a copy of the presentation is attached to the addendum agenda. They provided an overview of the key findings as provided in report CSD-HOU-23-024. P. Phillips noted that homelessness is a community issue that needs a community lead response. He further noted that they will be presenting a 2024 budget request in November. 

The Committee expressed support for the proposed Plan. In response to the Committee, Staff confirmed the importance of supportive services such as for mental health and addictions supports and that individuals can access supports more readily when they are housed. Staff also confirmed that the Working Group is focusing on community development which includes preparing for inclement weather with Community Partners.

The Committee requested that Staff provide 2024 budget recommendations on additional aid that may be necessary for individuals experiencing homelessness during inclement weather.

In response to the Committee, P. Phillips confirmed that Staff have been working on engaging the public through online communications and the implementation of education and dialogue resources. He also confirmed Staff will provide statistics on the number of individuals that are experiencing chronic homelessness. He further confirmed that the Working Team is actively monitoring the constantly changing experiences of individuals suffering from homelessness including refugees and asylum seekers.

The Committee expressed concern with the lack of affordable housing as it relates to chronic homelessness. 

Received for information.

items.title: PHP-PSV-23-006, Paramedic Services 2024 Pre-Budget Request
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner of Paramedic Services & Public Health, introduce the 2024 Pre-budget Request presentation, a copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. John Riches, Director/Chief of Paramedic Services, provided the presentation which highlighted that service enhancements are critical for paramedic services. These service enhancements require increased funding as set out in PHP-PSV-23-006. He further highlighted the mental health strategy which is meant to support a healthier workforce.

J. Riches requested that the Committee support the funding aligns with the high growth scenario. He also provided an overview of the paramedic services programs and partnerships including the Designated Offload Nurse program.

In response to the Committee, J. Riches explained that the pre-budget request is due to the continuation of offload delays. He also explained that response times are affected by the call demands and that 911 calls should hopefully be diverted with the assistance of the service enhancements that may be possible with the requested budget amount.

items.title: CAO-EDI-23-003, Amendment to Code of Use By-Law (13-050) to Prohibit Harassing/Discriminatory Behaviour on Regional Premises
notes:
Fauzia Baig, Director of Equity, Diversity, Inclusion presented on the report CAO-EDI-23-003, Amendment to Code of Use By-Law (13-050) to Prohibit Harassing/Discriminatory Behaviour on Regional Premises, a copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. She provided an overview of the background on the proposed amendment of the Code of Use By-law; which was recommended by the Coalition of Muslim Women Kitchener-Waterloo. Based on that recommendation the Municipal Anti-Hate working group coordinated an approach to facilitate this amendment and created a plan to update other municipal policies and by-laws to align with the proposed amendment. 

R. Brookes, Regional Senior Solicitor, explained the purpose of the Code of Use By-law and that the proposed amendment would add language under Schedule "B" of the By-law that would prohibit harassment based on the protected grounds of the Ontario Human Rights Code and would permit an offence enforcement strategy such as removal from Regional premises.

F. Baig continued by outlining the next steps, specifically, that Staff will coordinate with by-law enforcement Staff and Security Officers to identify training needs. She noted that the proposed amending by-law would become effective on January 1, 2024.

In response to the Committee, F. Baig confirmed that the working group can be expanded to add additional membership to ensure Township representation.

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with regard to Year 5 (2023/24) and 6 (2024/25) of the Canada-Ontario Community Housing Initiative (COCHI) and the Ontario Priorities Housing Initiative (OPHI), as outlined in report CSD-HOU-23-025 dated September 12, 2023:

  1. Approve the recommended Year 5 and 6 Investment Plan for submission to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing;
  2. Authorize the Commissioner, Community Services Department to execute such agreements and documentation in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as may be required to process the advance of funding for these programs;
  3. Authorize either the Assistant Director or Director, Housing Services, to execute and deliver all other documentation required by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing and the Region of Waterloo to allocate funding from COCHI and OPHI;
  4. Approve 2 new full time equivalent (FTE) positions as detailed in Report CSD-HOU-23-025 dated September 12, 2023 to be fully funded from COCHI and OPHI funding; and

  5. Request the provincial government allocate additional Canada-Ontario Housing Benefit funding dedicated towards households experiencing homelessness in Waterloo region.

motions.item_title: Councillor R. Deutschmann Notice of Motion
motions.text: WHEREAS intimate partner violence, often referred to as domestic violence, means any use of physical or sexual force, actual or threatened in an intimate relationship, including emotional and/or psychological abuse or harassing behaviour. Persons of any gender or sex can be victims of intimate partner violence; AND WHEREAS on the morning of September 22, 2015, Carol Culleton, Anastasia Kuzyk and Nathalie Warmerdam were murdered by a former intimate partner; AND WHEREAS on June 28, 2022, the jury in a Coroner’s Inquest held on these deaths (hereinafter referred to as the CKW Inquest), delivered 86 recommendations; AND WHEREAS every six days in Canada a woman is killed by her intimate partner; AND WHEREAS in Ontario in 2022, 52 women, or one every week, were victims of femicide; AND WHEREAS in Ontario in 2023, year-to-date, 30 women in 30 weeks were the victim of femicide; AND WHEREAS the prevalence of intimate partner violence in Waterloo Region has continued to increase steadily over the last decade with the Waterloo Regional Police Service: Attending more than 66,000 calls for service, or an average of 6,600 per year and over 17 per day Laying more than 35,000 charges, or an average of over 3500 per year Investigating the homicide, attempt homicide and manslaughter of 24 people by an intimate partner; AND WHEREAS, on any given night in Canada, 6000 women and children sleep in shelters because it is not safe for them at home; AND WHEREAS racialized women and Indigenous women experience disproportionately high rates of intimate partner violence, AND WHEREAS Indigenous women are approximately 3.5 times more likely to experience some form of intimate partner violence than non-Indigenous women, and the homicide rate for Indigenous women and girls is approximately 6 times higher than for non-Indigenous women and girls, and Indigenous women are 12 times more likely to be murdered or missing than any other women in Canada and 16 times more likely than white women; AND WHEREAS violence against women costs the justice system, health care systems, social services agencies and municipalities billions of dollars per year, and municipalities are on the front lines in addressing gender-based violence; AND WHEREAS Lanark County, the City of Ottawa, the Region of Durham, Burlington City Council, the Region of Peel, the City of Toronto and numerous other municipal councils, have passed motions declaring intimate partner violence an epidemic and acknowledging the 86 recommendations made by the CKW jury; AND WHEREAS Indigenous women and girls are 12 times more likely to be missing or murdered when compared to other women in Canada, and that number is 16 times when compared only with White women; AND WHEREAS the homicide rate for Indigenous community members was seven times higher than their non-Indigenous counterparts. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: THAT Waterloo Regional Council: Recognizes the issues of violence against women and girls in Waterloo Region as serious to the health and wellness of our residents and their families, AND Is committed to engaging with community partners to educate and support our residents about the seriousness and long-term danger of violence in our community; AND THAT Waterloo Regional Council declares that intimate partner violence and violence against women is an epidemic, in accordance with Recommendation #1 of the CKW Inquest; AND THAT the Province of Ontario be requested to declare that intimate partner violence and violence against women is an epidemic, in accordance with Recommendation #1 of the CKW Inquest; AND THAT Waterloo Regional Council agrees to integrate intimate partner violence into the Region’s Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, in accordance with Recommendation #10 of the CKW Inquest, and set out gender-based violence/intimate partner violence as a separate priority within the plan, AND THAT Waterloo Regional Council declares that Intimate Partner Violence and Violence Against Indigenous women, girls and 2SLGBTQQIA is an epidemic, AND THAT the Province of Ontario be requested to declare, that Intimate Partner Violence and Violence against Indigenous women, girls and 2SLGBTQQIA is an epidemic, AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT this resolution will be circulated to The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, The Honourable Charmaine A. Williams, Associate Minister of Women’s Social and Economic Opportunity, The Honourable Parm Gill, Minister of Red Tape Reduction, Members of Parliament and Members of Provincial Parliament representing Waterloo Region, all the cities and townships in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, the Waterloo Region Police Services Board, the Federation of Canadian Municipalities, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario and the Ontario Big City Mayors.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS intimate partner violence, often referred to as domestic violence, means any use of physical or sexual force, actual or threatened in an intimate relationship, including emotional and/or psychological abuse or harassing behaviour. Persons of any gender or sex can be victims of intimate partner violence; AND

WHEREAS on the morning of September 22, 2015, Carol Culleton, Anastasia Kuzyk and Nathalie Warmerdam were murdered by a former intimate partner; AND

WHEREAS on June 28, 2022, the jury in a Coroner’s Inquest held on these deaths (hereinafter referred to as the CKW Inquest), delivered 86 recommendations; AND

WHEREAS every six days in Canada a woman is killed by her intimate partner; AND

WHEREAS in Ontario in 2022, 52 women, or one every week, were victims of femicide; AND

WHEREAS in Ontario in 2023, year-to-date, 30 women in 30 weeks were the victim of femicide; AND

WHEREAS the prevalence of intimate partner violence in Waterloo Region has continued to increase steadily over the last decade with the Waterloo Regional Police Service:

  • Attending more than 66,000 calls for service, or an average of 6,600 per year and over 17 per day
  • Laying more than 35,000 charges, or an average of over 3500 per year
  • Investigating the homicide, attempt homicide and manslaughter of 24 people by an intimate partner; AND

WHEREAS, on any given night in Canada, 6000 women and children sleep in shelters because it is not safe for them at home; AND

WHEREAS racialized women and Indigenous women experience disproportionately high rates of intimate partner violence, AND

WHEREAS Indigenous women are approximately 3.5 times more likely to experience some form of intimate partner violence than non-Indigenous women, and the homicide rate for Indigenous women and girls is approximately 6 times higher than for non-Indigenous women and girls, and Indigenous women are 12 times more likely to be murdered or missing than any other women in Canada and 16 times more likely than white women; AND

WHEREAS violence against women costs the justice system, health care systems, social services agencies and municipalities billions of dollars per year, and municipalities are on the front lines in addressing gender-based violence; AND

WHEREAS Lanark County, the City of Ottawa, the Region of Durham, Burlington City Council, the Region of Peel, the City of Toronto and numerous other municipal councils, have passed motions declaring intimate partner violence an epidemic and acknowledging the 86 recommendations made by the CKW jury; AND

WHEREAS Indigenous women and girls are 12 times more likely to be missing or murdered when compared to other women in Canada, and that number is 16 times when compared only with White women; AND

WHEREAS the homicide rate for Indigenous community members was seven times higher than their non-Indigenous counterparts.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:

THAT Waterloo Regional Council:

Recognizes the issues of violence against women and girls in Waterloo Region as serious to the health and wellness of our residents and their families, AND

Is committed to engaging with community partners to educate and support our residents about the seriousness and long-term danger of violence in our community; AND

THAT Waterloo Regional Council declares that intimate partner violence and violence against women is an epidemic, in accordance with Recommendation #1 of the CKW Inquest; AND

THAT the Province of Ontario be requested to declare that intimate partner violence and violence against women is an epidemic, in accordance with Recommendation #1 of the CKW Inquest; AND

THAT Waterloo Regional Council agrees to integrate intimate partner violence into the Region’s Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, in accordance with Recommendation #10 of the CKW Inquest, and set out gender-based violence/intimate partner violence as a separate priority within the plan, AND

THAT Waterloo Regional Council declares that Intimate Partner Violence and Violence Against Indigenous women, girls and 2SLGBTQQIA is an epidemic, AND

THAT the Province of Ontario be requested to declare, that Intimate Partner Violence and Violence against Indigenous women, girls and 2SLGBTQQIA is an epidemic, AND

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT this resolution will be circulated to The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, The Honourable Charmaine A. Williams, Associate Minister of Women’s Social and Economic Opportunity, The Honourable Parm Gill, Minister of Red Tape Reduction, Members of Parliament and Members of Provincial Parliament representing Waterloo Region, all the cities and townships in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, the Waterloo Region Police Services Board, the Federation of Canadian Municipalities, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario and the Ontario Big City Mayors.
